answer:
Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin) to solve the small-strain linear elasticity problem in 2D plane stress on a rectangular plate of 1.0 m by 0.5 m with unit thickness.
The plate contains a central circular hole of radius 0.1 m centered at (0.5, 0.25), whose boundary remains traction-free.
Create an additional semicircular notch of radius 0.02 m open on the right edge of the plate, centered at (1, 0.25), spanning an angular extent of π rad; document this geometry as an assumption.
Mesh the domain with 64 elements per edge.
Use a vector-valued displacement space for the two displacement components.
Material properties: Young's modulus E = 70e9 Pa, Poisson's ratio ν = 0.33, density ρ = 2700 kg/m^3.
Use the reduced plane-stress constitutive law for the stress-strain relation.
Apply gravity as a body force b = (0, -ρg) with g = 9.81 m/s^2; document this direction as an assumption.
Apply the torque load as a tangential traction t_θ = M/(2πr) with M = 800 N·m and r = 0.02 m, acting only on the semicircular notch arc in the local tangential direction e_θ = (-sin θ, cos θ), adopting the counterclockwise sense; document this sense and the angular extent as assumptions.
Fix the left boundary with a full clamped condition u = 0 (both displacement components) along the entire left edge x = 0; document this as an assumption.
Solve the linear system with a direct linear solver.
Compute the in-plane Cauchy stress field from the plane-stress constitutive law.
Compute the von Mises stress field from the in-plane Cauchy stresses.
Save the displacement field and the von Mises field to an XDMF/PVD output file for visualization in ParaView.
Report the maximum displacement magnitude and its location, and the maximum von Mises stress and its location, as scalar summary results.
Document all assumptions (notch geometry and angular extent, torque sense, full clamping, gravity direction) in the output or code comments.
